ProblemStatement: Low-resource definition remains inconsistent across papers
WhyItMatters: Comparisons become weak when low-resource means different combinations of hours quality validation language and compute
CurrentEvidence: Core surveys and benchmark papers support a multidimensional definition
NearTermResearchNeed: State resource condition explicitly in each study
LongTermResearchNeed: Develop shared reporting schema for low-resource ASR
EvaluationRequirement: Report labeled hours unlabeled data validation metadata and compute
RiskIfIgnored: The paper may repeat vague low-resource terminology

ProblemStatement: Dataset size is often reported without enough quality validation metadata licensing or dialect information
WhyItMatters: Hours alone cannot show whether data supports reliable deployment
CurrentEvidence: Common Voice VoxPopuli Lau et al and AfriSpeech evidence show quality and metadata matter
NearTermResearchNeed: Add documentation fields for source quality dialect consent license and validation
LongTermResearchNeed: Adopt community-aware data statements or datasheets for speech corpora
EvaluationRequirement: Report validation protocol metadata coverage and access conditions
RiskIfIgnored: Benchmarks may look comparable while hiding data risk

ProblemStatement: Orthographic normalization and transcript comparability remain underreported
WhyItMatters: Text conventions can change WER CER and cross-study comparability
CurrentEvidence: Data-quality punctuation and lenient-evaluation evidence support the problem
NearTermResearchNeed: Publish normalization and scoring scripts with benchmark reports
LongTermResearchNeed: Develop language-aware scoring guidance for scripts and morphology
EvaluationRequirement: Report raw and normalized scoring when feasible
RiskIfIgnored: Reported gains may reflect formatting rather than recognition

ProblemStatement: Foundation-model results are often reported as aggregate scores hiding per-language dialect and domain failures
WhyItMatters: Average scores can hide the communities that low-resource ASR is meant to serve
CurrentEvidence: ML-SUPERB XTREME-S IndicSUPERB AfriSpeech and fairness evidence support subgroup reporting
NearTermResearchNeed: Require per-language and per-domain result tables
LongTermResearchNeed: Build dialect and domain benchmark suites with metadata
EvaluationRequirement: Report macro averages and subgroup distributions not only pooled means

ProblemStatement: Adaptation comparisons are not standardized across compute budgets data volumes and forgetting constraints
WhyItMatters: Readers cannot tell whether gains come from method choice data scale or compute
CurrentEvidence: Block D adaptation evidence supports conditional comparison
NearTermResearchNeed: Report adaptation data volume trainable parameters compute and forgetting tests
LongTermResearchNeed: Create matched adaptation leaderboards for low-resource ASR
EvaluationRequirement: Use fixed-budget and variable-budget evaluation protocols
RiskIfIgnored: The review may imply one best adaptation method

ProblemStatement: Parameter-efficient methods are promising but direct ASR evidence is uneven compared with NLP evidence
WhyItMatters: PEFT may be overpromoted without ASR-specific validation
CurrentEvidence: Adapters LoRA and QLoRA are strong method anchors but not all are ASR evidence
NearTermResearchNeed: Separate method anchors from ASR-specific evidence in prose
LongTermResearchNeed: Develop direct PEFT comparisons on multilingual ASR benchmarks
EvaluationRequirement: Report trainable parameters memory latency and ASR quality
RiskIfIgnored: NLP evidence may be incorrectly transferred to ASR

ProblemStatement: Pseudo-labeling can scale supervision but teacher errors and low-confidence labels remain a major reliability bottleneck
WhyItMatters: Noisy labels can amplify bias and domain mismatch
CurrentEvidence: Self-training noisy student DUST and low-resource pseudo-labeling support the claim
NearTermResearchNeed: Report teacher confidence calibration and filtering thresholds
LongTermResearchNeed: Develop pseudo-label quality benchmarks for low-resource speech
EvaluationRequirement: Evaluate pseudo-label quality by language domain and confidence bin
RiskIfIgnored: Pseudo-labels may be treated as clean supervision

ProblemStatement: Multi-teacher KD needs better disagreement analysis and reproducible selection rules
WhyItMatters: Teacher ensembles can improve coverage but disagreement can signal risk
CurrentEvidence: Self-adaptive distillation MUST and large-scale pseudo-label evidence support this gap
NearTermResearchNeed: Report teacher agreement metrics and selection rules
EvaluationRequirement: Compare agreement-based filtering against single-teacher baselines
RiskIfIgnored: KD claims may hide error propagation

ProblemStatement: WER/CER alone is insufficient for hallucination over-correction and contextual ASR evaluation
WhyItMatters: LLM-assisted ASR can rewrite semantically or hallucinate while improving surface metrics
CurrentEvidence: Careless Whisper and Block F watchlist sources support caution
NearTermResearchNeed: Use constrained N-best or lattice correction protocols and semantic checks
LongTermResearchNeed: Build accepted benchmarks for hallucination and correction drift in ASR
EvaluationRequirement: Report hallucination over-correction semantic drift and source-grounding metrics
RiskIfIgnored: LLM correction may be mistaken for reliable ASR improvement

ProblemStatement: Low-resource AVSR lacks multilingual or multidialect resources and comparable protocols
WhyItMatters: AVSR may help noisy speech but current resources are narrow
CurrentEvidence: AV-HuBERT robust AVSR and MuAViC support promise and limits
NearTermResearchNeed: Document language and modality coverage in AVSR datasets
LongTermResearchNeed: Create multilingual and dialect-aware AVSR benchmarks
EvaluationRequirement: Report audio-only visual-only and audio-visual results under noise
RiskIfIgnored: Multimodal claims may be overgeneralized from narrow settings

ProblemStatement: LLM-assisted ASR needs constrained correction or rescoring protocols to avoid unconstrained rewriting
WhyItMatters: Free generation can change meaning or add content
CurrentEvidence: Block F LLM correction and hallucination evidence supports the risk
NearTermResearchNeed: Restrict correction to ASR hypotheses lattices or validated context
LongTermResearchNeed: Develop guardrails for correction rescoring and post-ASR normalization
EvaluationRequirement: Measure semantic preservation and unsupported insertions
RiskIfIgnored: LLM outputs may be evaluated as recognition when they are rewriting

ProblemStatement: Reproducibility and compute reporting remain weak especially for foundation-scale models
WhyItMatters: Under-resourced communities may not be able to reproduce or deploy expensive systems
CurrentEvidence: SUPERB toolkit benchmark and PEFT evidence support compute-aware reporting
NearTermResearchNeed: Report model versions decoding settings hardware memory and inference cost
LongTermResearchNeed: Create compute-normalized reporting for low-resource ASR
EvaluationRequirement: Include accuracy cost reproducibility and deployment constraints
RiskIfIgnored: Claims may favor methods that are impractical outside large labs
